title: Manufacturing
description: Plan, release and record production using controlled inventory and accounting commands.

descriptions.work-orders: Production orders, materials, operations and finished output.
descriptions.work-centers: Resources, working capacity and effective machine rates.
descriptions.mrp: Review shortages, firm suggestions and create supply documents.

empty.work-orders: No work orders in this view
empty.work-centers: No work centers in this view
empty.mrp: No planning runs in this view

emptyNote.work-orders: Create an order, or change the filters to see existing production.
emptyNote.work-centers: Add a machine, labor resource or production cell.
emptyNote.routings: Create a routing and add its operations before activation.
emptyNote.mrp: Run MRP for a legal entity to review its supply suggestions.

fields.name: Name
fields.doneQty: Final good quantity for this operation

homeNote: Start with a produced item, a BOM and an active routing. Release freezes the production revision and cost evidence. Operators can then issue components, record operations and receive finished goods.
draftNote: Drafts are editable. Release freezes the BOM, routing and configured standard cost; it does not roll up a new standard from the BOM.
releasedNote: This order retains its released BOM, routing and costing evidence. New master revisions do not rewrite it.
mrpNote: MRP proposes supply from the saved inputs. Capacity is an advisory check; overloaded weeks do not shift planned dates.
issueNote: Select each component and its exact quantity. Tracked components need lot or serial choices. The posting command checks availability and holds at the issue location.
outputNote: This receipt adds finished quantity to inventory. Enter the quantity received now, its tracking and any required by-product valuation.
doneNote: Done closes execution and settles remaining WIP. Quantity tolerance, measured quantities and material requirements are enforced. Finished quantity below ordered quantity needs a short-completion reason, including orders with recorded scrap.
normalScrapNote: Record normal in-process production loss before the first finished-goods receipt. Its cost remains in WIP for the good output. This does not dispose stocked inventory. Abnormal losses or losses discovered after a receipt require holding the order for valuation review.
activateNote: Propose this draft for approval. Applying the approved event controls its effective window and ends an overlapping prior revision. Released work orders retain their own snapshots.
versionNote: The next draft copies the operations. Editing it cannot rewrite an already released work order.
operationNote: Start records the operation timestamp. Complete records its final good quantity and finish timestamp once, including configured backflush, labor and overhead. It is not an incremental production counter.
deleteOperationNote: Remove this operation from the draft routing. Released revisions remain unchanged.
convertNote: Conversion creates the native work order, purchase order draft or transfer instruction. The saved suggestion supplies quantity and dates.
capacityNote: These are the current weekly capacity facts for the run horizon, refreshed by later MRP runs. They are not an immutable historical schedule. Overload flags are the only scheduling claim.
suggestionNote: Select a suggestion to firm, convert or dismiss it. Buy conversion also requires the purchase-order creation grant. Superseded runs remain available for reference.
loadFailed: The manufacturing record could not be loaded.
commandFailed: The command was refused. Reload the record if the problem continues.
emptyChildrenNote: Related records appear here as this parent progresses.
issueLinesRequired: Add at least one component issue line.
trackingNote: Leave tracking empty for untracked output. Add a row for each lot allocation or individual serial, including tracked by-products. Serial quantities must be one. The receipt command validates the complete allocation.
byproductNote: Leave these blank to use each item’s configured default value. A manual value requires an explanation.
uncertain: The response was not confirmed. The command may have committed. Review the record and posting evidence before attempting another quantity change.

genealogy.title: Lot & serial genealogy
genealogy.association: Inputs are recorded or estimated for the receipt batch, not each individual output piece. Older receipts retain their work-order association.
genealogy.scoped: Only authorized legal entities are included.
genealogy.truncated: This trace reached its depth or size limit. Open a linked identity to continue.
genealogy.emptyNote: No unreversed posted production links were found in this trace.
genealogy.chooseNote: Open a tracked identity from a work order’s materials or finished receipts.

journey.draft: Review the product, quantity and routing, then release the order. Release keeps its BOM, routing and cost evidence.
journey.released: Start the order when the team is ready. Record material issues and operation progress as work happens.
journey.working: Continue the next operation. Employee hours and machine elapsed time can be captured separately.
journey.readyToReceive: Operations are complete. Record finished quantity and its lot or serial, then finish the order.
journey.finished: Production is finished. Detailed records and posting evidence remain available in the tabs.
journey.review: Review the current status and its reason before taking the next action.
journey.employeeTime: Record and approve employee hours in Production time before completing this operation.
journey.cancelled: This order was cancelled. Its history remains available; it is not completed production.
journey.remaining: {remaining} {unit} remain to be received after recorded scrap.
journey.shortClosed: Finished below expected good output: {remaining} {unit}. Review the recorded completion reason.
journey.allLoss: All planned output is recorded as scrap. Hold the order for disposition; no goods receipt will be created.
journey.disposedLoss: Work disposed through an approved loss.

cockpit.description: Choose the work style, run the queue and record only the detail your operation needs.
cockpit.firstTime: First production run? Review the setup journey.
cockpit.projectNote: Customer jobs that need time and progress can stay in Projects. Choose production when you need controlled material consumption and finished inventory.
cockpit.empty: Start production from a workflow card, or review company setup.

setupJourney.title: Set up the way you work
setupJourney.description: Start with a useful workflow. Departments can offer several styles; features and permissions remain the company’s authority.

workflows.title: Choose work styles
workflows.description: Use the standard cards or publish a tailored profile. Keep a simple job simple.

scope.title: Assign department choices
scope.description: Offer one or several workflows and choose a default, or ask each time.

items.title: Prepare products and materials
items.description: Set base units, tracking, costing and effective bills of material in the item records.

resources.title: Prepare work centers
resources.description: Define resources, departments, calendars, capacity and effective machine rates.

costing.title: Review labor and costing
costing.description: Reuse shared wage rates and burden policies. Configure the posting accounts required by your costing model.

routings.title: Prepare operations and revisions
routings.description: Create effective routings, select labor capture and approve revisions before production.

setupJourney.projectNote: Projects remain their own work family. A shop job can use employee time without field tickets, a manufacturing tab or a production order.
setupJourney.productionNote: Production uses controlled material consumption and finished inventory. The checks below apply to the selected product and legal entity.
setupJourney.diagnosticNote: These checks describe current configuration. Creating, releasing and posting still enforce live authority, availability and approval policies.

next.project: No production setup is required for this project workflow. Add employee time or optional planning when useful.
next.draft: You can create a draft now and finish the missing configuration before release.
next.release: The selected product has the configuration shown below. Create a draft; release also checks quantities, stock and approvals.

setupJourney.noStyles: No operating styles are available with your current access and enabled features. Review the company’s feature choices, or ask an administrator for access.

rollup.title: Standard-cost roll-up
rollup.description: Preview the current BOM, scrap allowances, labor and overhead. Propose a standard for governed approval; applying it revalues open stock and preserves released-order snapshots.
rollup.batchNote: Material, labor, overhead and by-product credit are batch totals. The proposed standard is per unit; setup is allocated over the entered batch quantity.
rollup.proposed: Proposal saved. Submit it through the configured Accounting event approval, then apply the approved event.

bomApproval.proposed: Revision proposed. Review and submit it for approval.
bomApproval.note: Manufacturing recipe changes require approval. Retain earlier lines, end their effectivity today or later, and add successors with a new start date. Released production retains its exploded revision.
bomApproval.authority: An unrestricted manufacturing and company setup manager must propose shared recipe changes.

receiptInputs.title: Receipt inputs
receiptInputs.capture: Record the component issues used for this receipt
receiptInputs.estimatedNote: Automatic allocation estimates inputs proportionally across receipt batches. Capture actual inputs when precise genealogy matters.
receiptInputs.recordedNote: Select the issued lots or serials and their quantities for this receipt batch. The final receipt must account for every remaining input, including normal loss.
receiptInputs.required: Add the component issues and quantities for this receipt.

quality.title: Quality
quality.description: Inspect incoming stock and production using frozen plans and controlled dispositions.
quality.held: Failed stock remains held until its disposition is recorded.
quality.limits: An out-of-range measurement always fails the inspection.
quality.emptyNote: Required receipt and operation plans create inspections as work is posted or started.
quality.failed: The inspection could not be saved.
quality.trackingNeeded: Choose the produced lot or serial
quality.followupNote: After recording production scrap, inspect the remaining good quantity before completing the operation.
quality.recordedNote: Inspection recorded against its frozen plan.
quality.sourceReversed: This receipt was reversed. Its inspection remains as history; inspect the replacement receipt.
quality.sourceStopped: This production order was cancelled. Its inspection remains historical evidence; no output may be received.
quality.receiptReworkNote: Creates a production draft using this approved operation and the failed receipt’s frozen acceptance criteria. Issue the original held stock, record the repair and receive the same lot or serial back.
quality.repairRoutingMissing: No approved repair operation is available. Add and approve a routing for this item in Manufacturing → Routings; a repair consumes the failed item rather than a new BOM.
quality.repairAccepted: This repair is complete and meets its original acceptance criteria. Independent stock and inspection holds still apply.
quality.repairDisposed: The original inspected stock was consumed and discarded through an approved production loss. No repaired output was received.
quality.additionalInspectionNote: Add another inspection for this operation while it is running. Inspect each produced identifier. A repeated inspection of the same lot or serial replaces its accepted quantity; it does not add coverage.

formula.help: Formula inputs scale to the stated output. Batch inputs charge once per production order. Quantities use each item’s inventory base unit.

subcontract.title: Vendor operations
subcontract.intro: Send company-owned components to a vendor, keep their value and traceability, and return progress to this work order.
subcontract.failed: The vendor operation could not be saved.
subcontract.assignNote: Choose an unfinished operation with manual material issue. Its released routing, costs and inspections stay on this order.
subcontract.custodyMissing: A company administrator must add a company-owned stock location of type Vendor custody and select its vendor in Company Setup → Stock locations.
subcontract.shipNote: Shipping retains company-owned inventory. Components enter WIP only when the vendor uses them.
subcontract.serviceNote: Post a dedicated service bill in Purchasing, then record its actual posted expense in this order’s WIP. Project subcontracts remain separate.
subcontract.billMissing: No eligible posted bill is available. Ask a payables operator to post the dedicated bill for this vendor and legal entity.
subcontract.returnNote: Record the actual quantity delivered. Optional component consumption uses the original shipments. Final delivery runs the operation’s inspection and completion controls; finished stock uses the order’s Receive action.
subcontract.finishedNote: Recorded deliveries and costs remain evidence. Receive finished stock from the work order after its inspections pass.
subcontract.componentsNote: Return all unused quantity from one shipment to its original source, preserving its remaining carried value.
subcontract.noUnused: No unused quantity remains on these shipments.
subcontract.empty: No vendor operation is assigned. Keep ordinary operations internal, or assign an eligible operation when outside processing is needed.
subcontract.actualTimeNote: Optional actual times replace the released estimates. Employee labor uses approved time records when configured.
subcontract.cancelNote: Cancel an assignment with no shipment, delivery or active cost. Its evidence is retained.
subcontract.correctionNote: Reverse the capitalization into WIP. The posted vendor bill and payable remain unchanged. Received finished stock must be reversed first.

lossDispositionNote: Record only the quantity actually discarded and time actually consumed. Unstarted work is cancelled. The order is held for an independent accounting approval; no finished inventory is received.
repairIssueNote: Issue the full failed receipt into this repair. Its original lot or serial and quantity are filled in automatically; all unrelated holds remain in force.
repairOutputNote: Receive the full repaired quantity with its original lot or serial. The repair operation must pass inspection before this receipt can post.
capacityFrozenNote: Calendar inputs and weekly capacity facts are retained from this run. Planned dates are unchanged; overload flags identify weeks for review and do not promise finite scheduling.
repairDraftNote: This repair keeps its original inspected quantity, source location and lot or serial. Change its schedule or repaired-output location here; use Quality or Close as loss to dispose failed repair work.
jointOutputNote: Joint outputs share production cost by their quantity and relative cost weight per base unit. The primary output has weight 1. NRV by-products retain their separate net realizable value treatment.

process.title: Process run
process.windowNote: Use the existing planned start and finish to bound a continuous run, with an expected output quantity. Partial receipts account for each run’s output. A campaign reference groups related runs in search; it does not pool costs or replace each run’s approved recipe.
process.balanceNote: Quantities are grouped by the current inventory base unit. Different units stay separate. The difference is recorded input minus all recorded good and secondary output, not an automatic scrap or physical mass calculation. Reversed movements are excluded.
process.emptyNote: Issue components and receive output to see the recorded balance.
process.carryover: Carry material into the next run
process.carryoverNote: Receive retained intermediate material as a traceable inventory item, then issue that item and its lot or serial into the next run. Quality holds still apply. Genealogy follows the actual receipt and issue; no unrecorded WIP or automatic financial carryover is assumed.
